[
  {
    "title": "OrdersController exposes every order with no authorization or ownership check",
    "file": "ExampleApp/Controllers/OrdersController.cs",
    "startLine": 18,
    "category": "security",
    "severity": "CRITICAL",
    "cwe": ["CWE-862", "CWE-639"],
    "snippet": "public class OrdersController : ApiController\n{\n    [HttpGet]\n    [Route(\"api/orders/{id}\")]\n    public IHttpActionResult GetOrder(int id)\n    {\n        return Ok(_repo.Find(id));\n    }\n}",
    "problem": "The controller declares no [Authorize] attribute and the action returns an object located purely by a client-supplied id, with no comparison against the caller's identity.",
    "impact": "An unauthenticated caller can enumerate id values and read every order in the system, including other customers' data.",
    "recommendation": "Register a global AuthorizeAttribute so the default is deny, then compare the resolved order's owner against a claim on the caller and return 403 on mismatch."
  },
  {
    "title": "Exception handler stores per-request header values in instance fields on a singleton",
    "file": "ExampleApp/Services/GlobalExceptionHandler.cs",
    "startLine": 16,
    "category": "reliability",
    "severity": "MEDIUM",
    "cwe": ["CWE-488"],
    "snippet": "private IEnumerable<string> listOfServiceCodes = new List<string>();",
    "problem": "IExceptionHandler is resolved once for the application lifetime, so per-request values written to instance fields are shared across concurrent requests.",
    "impact": "Under concurrent failures the audit trail attributes one request's service code to another request's exception, corrupting the forensic record.",
    "recommendation": "Make the fields local variables inside the handler method; they are never used across calls."
  }
]
